item: B3 — the generated questions against the v0.2 holdout (HU-TX-2)

hardware.NOT_the_published_bench_machine: V02_REPORT.md and BASELINES.md figures were measured on 2 vCPU Xeon (AVX-512) / 8 GB. Nothing here may be merged with those.

acceptance_criterion: the generated questions cover the 3 leaf edits needed after the v0.2 suite failure; record honestly whether answering them up front lets the candidate pass without a failed run, including if it does not

finding.why: The question that owns the three edited leaves is asked, but it instructs 'copy each item exactly as it is written', which yields the document's plurals; B2 enforces that and refuses the singular forms the v0.2 expert used. The runtime matches terms whole-word (quantity.rs find_term), so 'cables' never matches 'Cable C-4' and the first validation fails on val-09 exactly as v0.2's did.

who_answered.statement: The engineer recording this run, from the document. Not a domain expert.

chain.dataset: tx-tasks-v1 regenerated; all files match the digests in the tracked MANIFEST.json (read from git)

owning_question.quote: This procedure does not apply to motors, cables, generators or dry-type transformers; such requests are out of scope.
owning_question.question: The procedure says "This procedure does not apply to motors, cables, generators or dry-type transformers; such requests are out of scope." (halvorn-hu-tx-2.txt p.1 [231:316]; halvorn-hu-tx-2.txt p.1 [317:348]). What equipment does the procedure NOT cover? Copy each item exactly as it is written in that sentence.
owning_question.answer_note: words copied from the sentence; anything not in it is refused

second_finding_subject_length.question: The procedure says "Scope: oil-immersed distribution transformers rated up to and including 33 kV." (halvorn-hu-tx-2.txt p.1 [152:158]; halvorn-hu-tx-2.txt p.1 [159:230]). What equipment does the procedure cover? Copy the words exactly as they are written in that sentence.
second_finding_subject_length.reading: The question says to copy the words exactly but does not state the compiler's 32-character term limit, so the natural answer is refused. B2 is right to refuse (compile_ir does not enforce its own maxLength; the v0.2 model IR carried this 38-character term); the question should state the limit.

diagnostic_outside_b2.change: out_of_scope_terms replaced by the v0.2 expert's terms; nothing else
